statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-4437 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0005) is in the DNS backend of the GNU C Library (glibc), versions 2.34 to 2.43: gethostbyaddr and gethostbyaddr_r can treat a record from a non-answer section of a crafted DNS response as the answer, so the caller may be handed the wrong host name. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0005, https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=34014, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4437 (fixed for trixie in glibc 2.41-12+deb13u3). This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked all 51 binary packages published from the curl source in the DHI Debian repository as of 2026-11-27: three builds of curl 8.14.1, rebuilt from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 sources, for amd64 and arm64 (libcurl4-doc is architecture-independent), namely curl, libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libcurl4-gnutls-dev and libcurl4-doc, and the debug-symbol packages curl-dbgsym, libcurl4t64-dbgsym and libcurl3t64-gnutls-dbgsym. Their ELF files are the curl program and the libcurl.so.4.8.0 (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 (GnuTLS) shared libraries, each dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, with the curl program using the system dynamic loader as its interpreter, plus detached debug-information files in the debug-symbol packages. The development packages also ship the static archives libcurl.a (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.a (GnuTLS), each with 179 members that are all libcurl's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file. None of the packages contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, libpthread, libresolv, a gconv module, nscd or any other part of glibc, and no ELF file or archive member carries the GNU C Library version banner; the same scan of the DHI libc6 2.41-12+deb13u5 package finds libc.so.6, the loader and the banner. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package built from the glibc source, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4437 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0005, glibc bug 34014): in the GNU C Library 2.34 to 2.43, when nsswitch.conf uses the DNS backend, gethostbyaddr and gethostbyaddr_r ignored the answer-section boundary of a DNS response, so a crafted response from the configured DNS server could make the application treat records outside the answer section as valid answers. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0005. Upstream fixed it on the 2.41 branch in https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=commit;h=dbd8335c8ce8af11226ee1514d7a020b15c63345 (resolv: Count records correctly). Debian fixed it for trixie in 2.41-12+deb13u3 (Debian bug 1131435, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4437). The one glibc build published in the DHI Debian repository is Debian's 2.41-12+deb13u4 rebuilt for DHI, on amd64 and arm64; the version banner in its libc.so.6 names that Debian release (glibc 2.41). We checked the libc6 package of that build for both architectures against the repository index checksum: the Debian changelog it ships carries the 2.41-12+deb13u3 entry that applies the upstream stable-branch fix for CVE-2026-4437. The range ends at that build.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-4437 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0005) is in the DNS backend of the GNU C Library (glibc), versions 2.34 to 2.43: a defect in getanswer_ptr lets gethostbyaddr and gethostbyaddr_r, given a crafted response from the configured DNS server, treat a non-answer section of the response as the answer and return the wrong hostname. Debian fixed it in trixie in glibc 2.41-12+deb13u3. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0005, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4437. This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked every binary package published from the ncurses source in the DHI Debian repository for amd64 and arm64 (56 index entries in 50 distinct files, because the architecture-independent ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc are listed for both): both published rebuilds of Debian's ncurses 6.5+20250216-2 (libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, libncurses-dev, ncurses-bin, ncurses-base, ncurses-term, ncurses-doc and ncurses-examples, and the debug-symbol packages for libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, ncurses-bin and ncurses-examples). None of them contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, libpthread or another glibc library, a glibc gconv module, the glibc version banner, a statically linked program, a PE or Mach-O file, or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. The shared libraries (libtinfo, libtic, libncurses, libncursesw, libform, libformw, libmenu, libmenuw, libpanel and libpanelw) and the programs in ncurses-bin (clear, infocmp, tabs, tic, toe, tput and tset) and ncurses-examples are dynamically linked ELF files that list the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED, and the programs name the system dynamic loader (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 or ld-linux-aarch64.so.1) as their interpreter. libncurses-dev ships twelve static archives (libncurses.a, libncursesw.a, libtinfo.a, libtic.a, libform.a, libformw.a, libmenu.a, libmenuw.a, libpanel.a, libpanelw.a, libncurses++.a and libncurses++w.a, plus libcurses.a and libtermcap.a as symlinks to two of them) whose members are ncurses's own object files; a program that links them statically takes its C library from its own build, not from this package. The debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information, and ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc hold terminfo entries, tab-set files and documentation with no ELF files or archives. glibc reaches an image through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.
